package: @astryxdesign/cli

## Set up agent docs

Tell your AI to install the CLI and set itself up:

Paste this into your AI:
```text
Install @astryxdesign/cli and run `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 init --features agents` to set up your Astryx context. Read the generated file.
```

That's it. The `init --features agents` command generates everything your AI needs (component index, behavioral rules, CLI reference, and package guidance from configured integrations) from the installed project. After a dependency bump, `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 upgrade --from <old version>` reports a stale block and adding `--apply` refreshes it.

By default this writes the instructions to `AGENTS.md` (the tool-agnostic standard most agents read), in the project root: the nearest folder whose `package.json` declares an Astryx package, else the nearest with any `package.json`. The search stops at the repository root. In the home folder, or in a settings folder in it outside a project, init writes no agent docs: every folder of the home folder whose name starts with a dot (`~/.claude`, `~/.gemini`, `~/.codex`) is a settings folder, and such a folder itself never counts as a project, even with a `package.json`; a project below it with its own `package.json`, such as an agent worktree, is set up normally. Claude Code skips `AGENTS.md` when the project has a `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, so init also writes them to that file, even when it imports `AGENTS.md`: Claude Code does not follow that import in a session started in a subfolder. When both files exist, root `CLAUDE.md` gets the copy and a copy in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` is removed, unless the project ignores `CLAUDE.md`, in which case a `.claude/CLAUDE.md` the project commits keeps a copy. Gemini CLI reads only `GEMINI.md`, so init adds a one-line import of `AGENTS.md` there, unless `GEMINI.md` already imports it. `upgrade` keeps the copies in sync. The block between the Astryx markers belongs to Astryx: init and `upgrade` write, refresh, and remove it whatever the project's ignore rules or generated markers say, and never change the text around it. To target a specific tool's file instead:

Manual options:
```bash
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 init --features agents --agent claude    # CLAUDE.md if present, else .claude/CLAUDE.md
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 init --features agents --agent cursor    # .cursorrules if present, else AGENTS.md
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 init --features agents --agent codex     # AGENTS.md (Copilot, Codex, etc.)
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 init --features agents --agent hermes    # .hermes.md or HERMES.md if present, else AGENTS.md
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 init --features agents --agent muse      # AGENTS.md (Muse)
npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 init --features agents --agent all       # every agent file present except GEMINI.md, else AGENTS.md and .claude/CLAUDE.md
```

With `--agent all`, `GEMINI.md` keeps its one-line import of `AGENTS.md`. With `--agent claude` or `--agent all`, as by default, when `CLAUDE.md` gets the instructions, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` gets none and a copy already there is removed, unless the project ignores `CLAUDE.md`: a fresh clone does not have it, so a `.claude/CLAUDE.md` the project commits gets a copy too, with `--agent claude` and `--agent all` alike. `init --remove-agents` removes them at the project root and in the folder it runs in.

For agents that work outside any one project, your global install keeps one short Astryx skill, `~/.agents/skills/astryx/SKILL.md`, linked into the skill folders agent tools read, such as `~/.claude/skills/astryx`. It tells agents Astryx is there and when to use it; `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 init --user` writes it now or, with `--remove-agents`, turns it off. Inside a project, agents follow that project's own agent docs. See `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs global/computer-agent-guide`.
